bridge: Start with a fictional notes service. You can reason about its security on paper before installing any security tools.
teaching:
### Ask what must be protected

A private note should be readable only by the right people. That is confidentiality. Its contents should not be changed without permission. That is integrity. The service should also be usable when needed. That is availability.

These goals can conflict. A stricter sign-in check might protect notes but also lock out their owner if recovery is poorly designed. Security decisions need to consider the actual service and its users.

### Separate a weakness from an attack

A vulnerability is a weakness that can allow something unwanted. A threat is a possible harmful event. An attack is an attempt to cause it. For example, a missing ownership check is a weakness; someone using it to open another person's note is an attack.

A control is a step intended to reduce a risk, such as checking ownership on the server. Risk considers how likely an unwanted event is and what its consequences would be.

### Practise within a clear permission boundary

Use the named training lab, your own isolated system or the supplied fictional evidence. Ownership of a laptop does not give permission to test every service it can reach. A public website is not automatically a practice target.

Write down the permitted target, actions and time limits before testing. If an unexpected system or private record appears, stop that activity and follow the lab's reporting process. Reporting a suspected problem does not require publishing other people's data.

When you are inside the training folder, ../ means go up to its parent folder before locating the named file. In this paper task, training/readme.txt and training/answer.txt name files inside the target; ../payroll.csv names a file outside it. That takes the requested payroll file outside the training area. Scanning a website means probing its network services; it is a network action, not reading the permitted offline text files. You only classify these actions here.
example:
Fictional scope
Owner: local training instructor
Target: offline folder cyber-notes/training
Allowed: read and edit the supplied text files
Excluded: other folders, accounts and network services
Window: this practice session
Stop: any real personal information appears
Report: write a local incident note
explanation: Reading a supplied training file is within scope. Opening a sibling folder called payroll is outside scope even if the operating system permits it. Deleting training files might technically be an edit, but conflicts with the intent if destructive work was not agreed; seek a clearer scope. Finding personal data triggers the stop condition before further exploration.
exercise: For this exact scope, classify five actions: read training/readme.txt; edit training/answer.txt; open ../payroll.csv; scan example.org; stop after finding a real phone number. For each give permitted, prohibited or stop, plus one sentence tying the decision to scope.
solution: Read and edit are permitted within the stated training directory. Payroll and the scan are prohibited. The phone number requires stopping and a minimal local report. No network action is necessary to answer.
challenge:
Write a scope for an invented local note-taking app using these six headings: owner who grants permission; exact target; allowed actions; excluded actions and systems; time window; reporting route. Add a stop condition. Use fictional details and do not test an actual app.

Explain which security goal is harmed by (a) revealing a private note, (b) changing its owner without permission, (c) making notes unavailable. More than one goal can be affected; name the most direct one first.
challenge_solution:
One complete fictional scope is: owner—a local training instructor; target—the supplied offline training-notes folder; allowed—read the supplied notes and edit answer.txt; excluded—deletion, other folders, accounts and all networks; window—this practice session only; reporting route—a local incident-note.txt with a minimal description. Stop if unexpected personal information appears or the permitted action is unclear. Do not copy the private information into the report.

Revealing a private note harms confidentiality. Changing its owner without permission harms integrity and may also disclose it. Making notes unavailable harms availability. Permission for this offline folder does not cover any hosting service or external sign-in provider.
example_intro: This is an invented permission statement. Read it and classify the actions on paper. Do not open the excluded paths or scan a website to answer the question.
